slides.title: 3 military money benefits, explained
slides.sub: Official 2026 numbers from the pay tables, the VA and the Defense Department.

slides.heading: #1 Pay from day one
body: A new E-1 (the starting enlisted rank) earns $2,407.20 a month in basic pay in 2026, after a 3.8% raise in January. That's about $28,900 a year.
Basic pay is only part of it. Pay rises with rank and years served, and there are separate allowances for housing and food.

slides.heading: #2 Tuition paid later
body: After 36 months of active duty, the Post-9/11 GI Bill pays net in-state tuition and fees at public schools (the 100% level), plus up to $1,000 a year for books.
Going private? The cap is $30,908.34 a year for 2026 to 2027. Net means after scholarships and grants.

slides.heading: #3 A retirement match
slides.big: Up to 5% of basic pay added
body: The service puts 1% of your basic pay into a Thrift Savings Plan (TSP) retirement account, starting 60 days in, even if you put in nothing.
After 2 years, it matches what you put in, up to 5% total. Put in 5% and 10% of your basic pay goes to retirement.
slides.source: Air Force benefits page, reviewed Jan. 30, 2026

slides.takeaway: Big benefits come with a multi-year commitment. Talk to a recruiter and a veteran first.

posts.caption:
Thank you to everyone who has served. For Veterans Day, here's what military service pays, using official 2026 numbers.

1. Pay from day one: a new E-1 earns $2,407.20 a month in basic pay in 2026 (after a 3.8% raise), about $28,900 a year, plus separate allowances for housing and food.
2. College later: after 36 months of active duty, the Post-9/11 GI Bill covers net in-state tuition and fees at public schools at the 100% level, plus up to $1,000 a year for books. Private schools are capped at $30,908.34 a year for 2026 to 2027.
3. A retirement match: the service puts 1% of your basic pay into a Thrift Savings Plan account, and after 2 years it matches what you put in, up to 5% total.

These benefits come with a multi-year service commitment. Talk to a recruiter and a veteran before you decide.

Data: DFAS 2026 basic pay (via Military.com), VA Post-9/11 GI Bill rates (Aug. 1, 2026), Air Force Blended Retirement System page (reviewed Jan. 30, 2026).
